## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | Reviewers are blinded from authors and manuscripts "should be blinded" for author identity as far as possible: double-anonymous in effect. Editorial pre-screening for priority and fit; the usual practice is two reviewers, more if needed; revisions usually go through the same process |
| **Transferable / Cascade?** | Not stated |
| **Reviewer reports published?** | Not stated |
| **Typical R+R rounds** | Not stated (revisions are "usually subject to the same process") |
| **Reviewer recommendations** | Authors must suggest at least four referees, excluding the PPP editors, whose affiliations should all be different from that of the authors (not for commentaries; Hopkins Press guidelines, snapshot 2026-10-16); authors may name reviewers they prefer to avoid; selection stays with the editors |

> Source: Hopkins Press Author Guidelines, Wayback snapshot 2026-10-16 of https://www.press.jhu.edu/journals/philosophy-psychiatry-psychology; Editor-in-Chief and ScholarOne submission at https://inpponline.com/publications/ppp/ (retrieved 2026-11-23). Reviewers may not put articles into generative-AI tools (same guidelines).

### AI Policy

## Format

Source for this section: Hopkins Press Author Guidelines, Wayback snapshot 2026-10-16 of https://www.press.jhu.edu/journals/philosophy-psychiatry-psychology (the live page returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch). Submission via ScholarOne (https://inpponline.com/publications/ppp/, retrieved 2026-11-23).

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Article types accepted** | Feature articles; Philosophical Case Conference (target article with commentators); review articles (topic approved by editors first; no book reviews); Key Concepts (encyclopedia-style, usually by invitation); commentaries and responses (by editorial invitation only) |
| **Word limit** | Feature articles typically 3,000-7,000 words; review articles 5,000-8,000; Key Concepts about 3,000 and at most 4,000; commentaries and responses 1,000-1,500. The word count submitted includes abstract, notes and references |
| **Word limit negotiability** | Longer feature articles "may be considered" if appropriate and justified to the editors and reviewers; longer commentaries need advance approval |
| **Abstract limit** | 150-250 words for features (none for commentaries); up to 6 keywords not already in the title; title at most 120 characters |
| **Reference limit** | Feature articles 40 entries unless a cover letter justifies more; reviews no limit; Key Concepts 15; commentaries 12. APA style, American spelling, footnotes not permitted, endnotes kept to 5-8 at most |
| **Supplementary material** | Not stated |
| **Figure/Table limits** | No numeric limit stated; each table or figure as a separate file |

### Orientation

> Keyword counts below are from Crossref records for ISSN 1086-3303 dated 2021-01-01 to 2026-11-23: 466 records (all typed journal-article), of which 139 (30%) carry a deposited abstract. Counts are of titles plus abstracts among the 139, matched locally, so they are lower bounds and are weak for this journal; title-only counts over all 466 are given where useful. Retrieved 2026-11-23. OpenAlex `works` queries were refused that day (daily budget used up).

| Dimension | Assessment |

| **Empirical vs. Theoretical** | Conceptual/phenomenological terms dominate the abstracts: "conceptual" 36 of 139 (25.9%), "phenomenolog*" 28 (20.1%), "histor*" 21 (15.1%); "empirical" 18 (12.9%), but the word also appears in papers that discuss empirical findings philosophically. The journal's own aims say submissions are "of a conceptual and reflective nature" |
| **Quantitative vs. Qualitative** | Few method terms: "qualitative" 6 (4.3%), "interview" 6 (4.3%), "quantitative" 6 (4.3%), "survey/questionnaire" 4 (2.9%), "experiment" 2 (1.4%), "statistical analysis/test/model" 0 |
| **Cross-disciplinary openness** | The journal's page invites contributions from medicine, neuroscience, social science, anthropology, nursing, law and religious studies; the board lists psychiatry, philosophy and psychology as its disciplines (Reviewer Pool Characteristics) |

**Current positioning (what the journal accepts now):** the aims on the Hopkins Press page describe the overlap of philosophy with psychiatry and clinical psychology, with the goals of clarifying philosophical aspects of practice and making clinical phenomena accessible to philosophers. The earlier pass's reading of 2024-2026 issues (phenomenological psychopathology, value-based models of depression, diagnostic reification, philosophy of eating disorders, a cluster on psychedelics) is retained as an earlier AI-research observation; the Crossref titles agree on psychedelics ("psychedeli*" in 10 of 466 titles, 2.1%).

**Methods noted as welcome (qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** conceptual and phenomenological analysis; philosophical case conferences with commentaries; review articles of the literature; clinical case material that is anonymised ("highly valued" when clinically relevant, per the guidelines); empirical work provided it "contain[s] substantive philosophical content".

## Soft Metadata

### Epistemological & Political Leanings

- Stated scope: PPP "publishes original submissions of a conceptual and reflective nature" drawing on empirical, historical and clinical material (Hopkins Press page, https://www.press.jhu.edu/journals/philosophy-psychiatry-psychology, Wayback snapshot 2026-10-16). No political stance is stated; the guidelines require "the principle of equal dignity of all persons" and inclusive, non-stigmatising language (https://www.press.jhu.edu/journals/philosophy-psychiatry-psychology, snapshot 2026-10-16).
- Terms in titles/abstracts, 139 records with abstracts 2021-2026 (Crossref, retrieved 2026-11-23): "phenomenolog*" 28 (20.1%), "hermeneutic*" 7 (5.0%), "enactiv*/embodied" 10 (7.2%), "psychoanaly*" 10 (7.2%), "neuro*" 9 (6.5%), "epistemic injustice" 6 (4.3%), "pragmati*" 5 (3.6%).
- Named thinkers in the same 139: Wittgenstein 5 (3.6%), Heidegger 4 (2.9%), Merleau-Ponty 4 (2.9%), Jaspers 4 (2.9%), Foucault 3 (2.2%), Kant 2 (1.4%), Husserl 0 (title-only count over all 466 records: 1).
- Reading of the counts: phenomenological and clinical-conceptual vocabulary is the largest single strand, with no single thinker above about 4%; this describes what is published, not editors' politics. Abstract coverage is only 30%, so the picture is partial.
- OpenAlex topics (spine, 2026-07-13): Mental Health and Psychiatry 787, Psychotherapy Techniques and Applications 301, Neuroethics, Human Enhancement, Biomedical Innovations 86.

### Framing Requirements

- Mandatory framing: submissions must sit in the overlap of philosophy and psychiatry/clinical psychology; empirical work "should nonetheless contain substantive philosophical content"; clinical relevance is "highly valued" (Hopkins Press Author Guidelines, https://www.press.jhu.edu/journals/philosophy-psychiatry-psychology, Wayback snapshot 2026-10-16).
- Audience framing: because the journal is transdisciplinary, authors "should adopt a style that is accessible to PPP's readers from various disciplines"; assume a reader with the background of a well-educated university graduate (https://www.press.jhu.edu/journals/philosophy-psychiatry-psychology, snapshot 2026-10-16).
- Article types and routes: features, philosophical case conferences and review articles are open submissions (review topics pre-approved by editors); Key Concepts and commentaries are normally commissioned by the editors (https://inpponline.com/publications/ppp/, retrieved 2026-11-23).
- Consequence of ignoring the format rules: "improperly formatted manuscripts will be returned to the author(s), and may be declined for future consideration" (https://www.press.jhu.edu/journals/philosophy-psychiatry-psychology, snapshot 2026-10-16). No desk-reject rate is published; SciRev has 0 reviews (https://scirev.org/reviews/philosophy-psychiatry-and-psychology/).

### Voice & Style

- Style rules (Hopkins Press Author Guidelines, https://www.press.jhu.edu/journals/philosophy-psychiatry-psychology, Wayback snapshot 2026-10-16): APA reference style, American spelling, double-spaced Times 12-point, no footnotes, endnotes at most 5-8, do not title the first section "Introduction", do not number sections, boldface major headings and boldface-italic subheadings.
- Abstract: 150-250 words stating the need, problem or main argument, approach and conclusions; up to 6 keywords not in the title; title at most 120 characters (https://www.press.jhu.edu/journals/philosophy-psychiatry-psychology, snapshot 2026-10-16).
- Register: accessible to readers from several disciplines; clear paragraph structure; technical terms must be explained; a concluding section that "avoids introducing new material" (https://www.press.jhu.edu/journals/philosophy-psychiatry-psychology, snapshot 2026-10-16).
- First-person use in abstracts: 88 of 139 abstracts (63%) contain "I", "my", "we" or "our" (case-sensitive local match on Crossref abstracts 2021-2026, retrieved 2026-11-23); first person is the norm, e.g. "In this paper, we examine..." (DOI 10.1353/ppp.2026.a1000146).
- Recent openings sampled (DOIs): 10.1353/ppp.0.a1003920 opens with the DSM definition of a diagnosis; 10.1353/ppp.0.a1003921 opens by engaging another author's 2025 formulation; 10.1353/ppp.0.a1003922 opens with a general claim about mindfulness interventions; 10.1353/ppp.0.a1003923 opens by defining a proposed diagnostic construct; 10.1353/ppp.2026.a1000145 opens "This manuscript undertakes an interdisciplinary investigation".

### Reviewer Pool Characteristics

- Review model: reviewers blinded to authors; manuscripts anonymised as far as possible; two reviewers usual, editors may obtain more; reviewers are barred from using generative-AI tools on manuscripts (Hopkins Press Author Guidelines, https://www.press.jhu.edu/journals/philosophy-psychiatry-psychology, Wayback snapshot 2026-10-16).
- Editorial board section of https://www.press.jhu.edu/journals/philosophy-psychiatry-psychology, snapshot 2026-10-16 (own count): 1 founding editor, 1 Editor-in-Chief (Werdie van Staden, University of Pretoria), 6 senior editors, 1 managing editor, 39 editorial board members, plus an advisory board of about 20 names with a chair.
- Disciplinary labels on the board entries (text count of the page): "Psychiatry" appears 21 times, "Philosophy" 19, "Psychology" 8, often in combination, so the pool is mixed clinical and philosophical.
- Countries named for board entries: 15 distinct countries (USA 12 entries and UK 9 are largest; then France 3, Canada 2, Germany 2, Poland 2; one each for Australia, Brazil, Bulgaria, Colombia, Denmark, Finland, Italy, Netherlands, New Zealand). Two entries name no country; counts come from a regex over the page text and may be off by one or two.
- Authors choose the pool partly: at least four suggested referees are required for non-commentary submissions, and their affiliations should all differ from the authors' affiliation (https://www.press.jhu.edu/journals/philosophy-psychiatry-psychology, snapshot 2026-10-16).
- OpenAlex topic mix (spine, 2026-07-13): Mental Health and Psychiatry 787, Psychotherapy Techniques and Applications 301.
- Reviewer behaviour itself (tone, turnaround, expectations) is not observable from public pages; SciRev has 0 reviews.

### Practical Concerns

- Ethics: the separate declarations document must address ethics approval and informed consent (or state they do not apply); where applicable they are also described in the text; PPP follows COPE and ICMJE guidance (Hopkins Press Author Guidelines, https://www.press.jhu.edu/journals/philosophy-psychiatry-psychology, Wayback snapshot 2026-10-16).
- Clinical cases: case material must be anonymous and non-identifiable; the person described should not be able to recognise themselves (https://www.press.jhu.edu/journals/philosophy-psychiatry-psychology, snapshot 2026-10-16).
- Declarations required with submission: ethics, conflicts of interest and funding, generative-AI use, accuracy of all references (no AI "ghost" references), at least four suggested referees, a biographical paragraph of at most 100 words per author (https://www.press.jhu.edu/journals/philosophy-psychiatry-psychology, snapshot 2026-10-16).
- Preprints: allowed before submission (originality condition quoted in the Preprint Policy table).
- Copyright and charges: copyright assigned to Johns Hopkins University Press on acceptance; no submission fee; optional OA fee USD 3,000 (https://www.press.jhu.edu/journals/philosophy-psychiatry-psychology, snapshot 2026-10-16).
- Indexing listed on the page: Web of Science Emerging Sources Citation Index, Scopus (from 2011), PsycINFO (from 1994), The Philosopher's Index (https://www.press.jhu.edu/journals/philosophy-psychiatry-psychology, snapshot 2026-10-16).
- Independent-scholar rules: not stated on the pages read (checked 2026-11-23); institutional affiliation is requested in the declarations document, but no eligibility requirement was found.

## Strategic Notes

> Every statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Judgements about the journal's culture are not made because the evidence for them is absent.

### Hard Blockers

- A manuscript that is not anonymised as far as possible: reviewers are blinded (Peer Review table).
- Work already published or under simultaneous consideration elsewhere; a preprint is the stated exception (Preprint Policy table).
- No declaration document, or missing ethics, funding, AI or reference-accuracy declarations (Practical Concerns).
- No four suggested referees, with affiliations different from the authors', for a non-commentary submission (Peer Review table).
- Empirical content without substantive philosophical content (Framing Requirements).

### Soft Tax

- Formatting: improper formatting can lead to return of the manuscript; no footnotes, no numbered sections, no "Introduction" heading, APA and American spelling (Voice & Style, Framing Requirements).
- Length discipline: 40-reference cap for features unless justified in a cover letter, and the word count includes abstract, notes and references (Format).
- Open access costs USD 3,000 if chosen; copyright goes to the Press (Open Access, Practical Concerns).
- Timeline unknown: no decision time is stated and SciRev has 0 reviews (Review Cycle Time).

### Best Suited For

- Conceptual or phenomenological analysis of a clinical problem: "conceptual" in 25.9% and "phenomenolog*" in 20.1% of abstracts (Orientation, Methodological Preferences).
- Authors who can write first-person argument for a mixed clinical-and-philosophical readership: 63% of sampled abstracts use first person; the page asks for accessible style (Voice & Style).
- Papers with anonymised clinical material: the guidelines say clinical relevance is "highly valued" (Framing Requirements).
- Review articles that integrate several books and articles: the editors say they are "keen" on more (Format, Framing Requirements).

### Not Recommended For

- A stand-alone quantitative or experimental study: "quantitative" appears in 4.3% and "experiment" in 1.4% of abstracts, and empirical work must contain philosophical content (Methodological Preferences, Framing Requirements); this is rarity plus a stated condition, not a ban.
- Authors needing a fast, predictable decision: nothing is stated and no review data exist (Review Cycle Time).
- Topic-focused work on race, gender or colonialism in mental health: each is 0-1.4% of abstracts (Sensitive Topics); this shows rarity in the sample, not editorial hostility.
